$$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

 

And the quotient rule is

$$
\frac{\text{d}(\frac{u}{v})}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}}
$$

Using the quotient rule, chain rule, and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{(\operatorname{artanh}⁡{x}^{2})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{artanh}⁡{x}^{2}\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{artanh}⁡{x}^{2})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}}-\frac{\operatorname{artanh}⁡{x}^{2}\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{artanh}⁡{x}^{2})}^{′}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}-\frac{\operatorname{artanh}⁡{x}^{2}}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}}\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{1-{({x}^{2})}^{2}}\cdot {({x}^{2})}^{′}-\frac{\operatorname{artanh}⁡{x}^{2}}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{1-{x}^{4}}\cdot 2x-\frac{\operatorname{artanh}⁡{x}^{2}}{x{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2x}{(1-{x}^{4})\operatorname{ln}⁡x}-\frac{\operatorname{artanh}⁡{x}^{2}}{x{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$
